providers.title: OpenAI models, hands on
providers.intro: Match the model to the job. Compare Astra, Sol, Terra, and Luna, estimate a real workload, connect the tools you need, and complete seven practical missions.
providers.simple: Astra tackles the hardest work. Sol balances capability and cost. Terra is geared toward visual work, computer interaction, and writing. Luna handles focused work that repeats.
providers.technical: The current flagship catalog lists text-and-image input, text output, approximately 1.05M context, and 128K maximum output for these four models. Supported effort levels differ: Astra and Sol start at low; Terra and Luna also offer none.

models.cardCopy: For visual reasoning, computer use, concise writing, and scoped code changes.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.cardCopy: For classification, routing, extraction, and other focused tasks at volume.

providers.title: Gemini models, hands on
providers.intro: Choose a reasoning model, a fast execution model, or a specialist for voice and media. Compare the results on text, documents, and visual inputs, then price the workflow you actually run.
providers.simple: Carbon is the strongest reasoning option in the current Gemini 4 catalog. Argon is the more efficient Gemini 4 option. Flash and Flash-Lite offer additional choices for repeated work. Voice and generated media have dedicated models.
providers.technical: Carbon accepts text, image, video, audio, and PDF and returns text. Its 1,048,576-token context is a unified input/output limit. Default synchronous output is 65,536 tokens; long decode supports more under its documented workflow. Carbon supports tools and structured output, but does not itself provide image generation, audio generation, or the Live API.

Thinking tokens are included in output billing. Editorial verification note: the live pricing page rendered its headings but not numeric tables during this review. Reconfirm these indexed rates before enabling the calculator. Carbon has no verified numeric rate in this pack.
providers.benchmarkCopy: Give each compatible model the same document, screenshot, and short video question. Score evidence location, factual correctness, omissions, latency, and cost. Test audio understanding separately from voice generation so the lab measures the intended capability.
providers.pattern: Suggested pattern: a compatible efficient model extracts candidate facts from each input, Argon synthesizes them, and Carbon handles difficult exceptions. Keep evidence locations alongside extracted facts so a reviewer can verify the final answer.

Tool support varies: Carbon’s support for audio input does not mean it generates speech. Present the specific endpoint and capability needed for every mission.

providers.title: Grok, hands on
providers.intro: Separate the reasoning model from its search tools. Compare a supplied-evidence answer with a grounded answer, then measure the cost of the complete workflow.
providers.simple: Grok 4.7 is the general-purpose flagship. Imagine and Voice cover other output types. Current information requires the relevant search tools.
providers.technical: The model catalog lists Grok 4.7 with 500K context and configurable reasoning. Web Search and X Search supply current information; the model alone is not a live feed.

providers.simple: Large 4 is the general-purpose multimodal flagship. Small 4 combines instruction following, reasoning, and coding in a smaller option. Specialist OCR and audio services address different jobs.
providers.technical: Large 4’s current card lists 1M context and an open-weight release under the Mistral Ecosystem Open Weight License. The card now says GA; the older October 6 changelog describes its earlier preview state. Use the current model card for present availability.

providers.title: Kimi models, hands on
providers.intro: Explore long-context coding and document work, distinguish product subscriptions from API usage, and measure a long task with explicit evidence and stopping conditions.
providers.simple: Kimi K3.1 Pro is Moonshot’s current flagship for demanding agentic work. K3 provides another model to compare. Use an exact ID and verify access before starting.
providers.technical: K3-series documentation lists a 1,048,576-token context window. K3.1 Pro uses the ID kimi-k3.1-pro, always enables thinking, and accepts low, high, or max reasoning effort, defaulting to max. A high-speed variant is separately listed.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.cardCopy: For demanding long-horizon coding and complex agentic work.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.cardCopy: A second K3-series baseline for your task set.

providers.pickerNote: Suggested evaluation path. Do not assume that a product subscription grants equivalent API credit or identical model access.
providers.costCopy: No numeric Kimi rates are asserted in this pack: the readable inference-pricing page did not expose a rate table. It does state that supported K3 batch requests are billed at 60% of standard pricing, and that caching can add TTL-dependent write charges. Verify the complete rate before enabling calculation.
providers.benchmarkCopy: Use a long document with facts planted near the beginning, middle, and end, plus a repository change with explicit regression tests. Measure retrieval accuracy and completed work rather than prompt capacity alone.
providers.pattern: Suggested pattern: inspect and index the evidence, plan the task, execute bounded steps, and stop at defined checkpoints. Keep a ledger of evidence, changed files, tests, and remaining uncertainty.
providers.access: The Pro quickstart says the flagship unlocks after a successful top-up of at least $1. API inference is pay-as-you-go and separate from Kimi membership and Kimi Code. Check the exact account and endpoint rather than assuming product access transfers.
